examples.en: The judge sentenced the defendant to two years in prison.

examples.ko: 법원은 내일 오전에 결과를 선고할 거예요.
examples.en: The court will announce its ruling tomorrow morning.
The judge's voice was quiet as he handed down the sentence.
The family cried when the court pronounced a not-guilty verdict.

examples.ko: 법원이 벌금을 선고한 사건이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: A case in which the court imposed a fine was on the news.

examples.ko: 오늘 재판이 끝나면 바로 형을 선고해요?
examples.en: Will they hand down the sentence right after today's trial ends?

explain: 재판에서 판사가 판결이나 형벌을 공식적으로 말할 때만 쓰는 말이라서 뉴스에서 '징역 3년을 선고했다'처럼 자주 나와요. 일상에서 '말하다' 대신 쓰지 않아요. '형을 선고하다', '무죄를 선고하다'처럼 판결 내용이 목적어로 와요.
explain_en: This word is used almost only when a judge officially announces a ruling or punishment in court, so you see it in news like '징역 3년을 선고했다' (sentenced to three years). Do not use it as a general word for 'say' or 'announce' in daily talk. The object is the content of the ruling, as in '형을 선고하다' (hand down a sentence) or '무죄를 선고하다' (declare not guilty).

en: load (onto a ship or plane); install, equip (a feature)

examples.en: This phone comes equipped with a new camera.

examples.ko: 화물을 배에 탑재하는 데 하루가 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a day to load the cargo onto the ship.

examples.ko: 새 차에 인공지능 기능을 탑재할 거예요.
examples.en: They will install an AI feature in the new car.

examples.ko: 새로 나온 노트북은 빠른 칩을 탑재해서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: The new laptop is popular because it has a fast chip built in.

examples.ko: 비행기에 짐을 탑재하기 전에 무게를 재요.
examples.en: They weigh the luggage before loading it onto the plane.

examples.ko: 탑재한 프로그램이 너무 많아서 컴퓨터가 느려요.
examples.en: The computer is slow because it has too many programs installed.

explain: 짐을 배나 비행기에 실을 때도 쓰지만, 요즘은 '기능을 탑재하다'처럼 제품 소개에서 더 자주 들려요. 말할 때는 '넣다', '들어 있다'가 더 흔해요. 사람을 태울 때는 '탑재하다'가 아니라 '태우다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used for loading cargo onto a ship or plane, but nowadays you hear it more in product descriptions like '기능을 탑재하다' (to be equipped with a feature). In casual speech, '넣다' or '들어 있다' is more common. For people, use '태우다' (to give a ride), not '탑재하다'.

en: struggle; fight (against hardship or for a cause)

examples.ko: 그는 병과 투쟁하면서도 웃음을 잃지 않았어요.
examples.en: He kept smiling even while fighting his illness.

examples.ko: 노동자들이 더 나은 월급을 위해 투쟁했어요.
examples.en: The workers struggled for better pay.

examples.ko: 어려운 환경과 투쟁하는 사람들의 이야기를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read stories about people struggling against hard conditions.

examples.ko: 시민들은 환경을 지키려고 끝까지 투쟁할 거예요.
examples.en: The citizens will fight to the end to protect the environment.

examples.ko: 부당한 대우에 맞서 투쟁한 사람이 상을 받았어요.
examples.en: A person who fought against unfair treatment received an award.
It is a family that has long struggled against poverty.

explain: '싸우다'는 일상 말이고, '투쟁하다'는 병, 가난, 부당한 일처럼 큰 대상과 오래 맞서는 느낌이에요. 친구와 다툴 때는 쓰지 않아요. 보통 '~와/과 투쟁하다', '~에 맞서 투쟁하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: '싸우다' is the everyday word for fighting. '투쟁하다' feels heavier: a long struggle against something big like illness, poverty, or unfair treatment. Do not use it for a quarrel with a friend. It usually appears as '~와/과 투쟁하다' or '~에 맞서 투쟁하다'.

examples.en: This school trains excellent cooks.

examples.ko: 정부가 젊은 과학자를 양성하려고 지원금을 줬어요.
examples.en: The government gave funding to nurture young scientists.
I want to attend a university that trains teachers.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 신입 사원을 전문가로 양성했어요.
examples.en: Our company trained its new employees to become experts.

examples.ko: 축구 선수를 양성할 학원이 우리 동네에 생겼어요.
examples.en: An academy to train soccer players opened in our neighborhood.
It takes a long time to develop talented people.

explain: '가르치다'는 지식을 알려 주는 것이고, '양성하다'는 어떤 일을 할 사람으로 키워 내는 것이에요. 목적어는 사람이고 '인재', '전문가', '선수'와 자주 같이 써요. 집에서 아이를 키울 때는 '키우다'를 써요.
explain_en: '가르치다' means to teach knowledge, while '양성하다' means to raise people into those who can do a certain job. The object is a person, often '인재' (talent), '전문가' (expert), or '선수' (athlete). For raising a child at home, use '키우다'.

examples.en: The game was stopped because of the rain.
The street has been quiet since the construction was halted.
Elevator service stops when the power goes out.
The service is scheduled to be suspended for a while.

examples.ko: 회사 전산망이 갑자기 중지되어서 일을 못 했어요.
examples.en: The company network was suddenly shut down, so I could not work.

examples.ko: 사고 때문에 지하철 운행이 중지되었다고 해요.
examples.en: I heard subway service was suspended because of an accident.

explain: 하던 일이 어떤 이유로 멈출 때 써요. 누가 일부러 멈추면 '중지하다', 일이 저절로 또는 사정 때문에 멈추면 '중지되다'예요. 뉴스와 안내문에서는 '중단되다'도 같은 뜻으로 많이 나와요.
explain_en: Use it when something that was going on stops for some reason. When someone stops it on purpose, it is '중지하다'; when it stops by circumstance, it is '중지되다'. In news and notices, '중단되다' is also commonly used with the same meaning.

examples.en: This snack is made from processed ingredients.
Milk is processed at a factory and then comes to the store.
Unprocessed wood is cheap.
Please check whether this photo has been edited.

examples.ko: 가공된 식품을 너무 많이 먹지 마세요.
examples.en: Do not eat too much processed food.

examples.ko: 철이 가공되면 여러 가지 물건이 돼요.
examples.en: When iron is processed, it becomes many kinds of things.

explain: '가공식품'처럼 원료에 손을 대서 바꾼 것에 써요. 사진이나 영상이 '가공되다'라고 하면 꾸며서 원래와 달라졌다는 뜻도 있어요. 손대지 않은 것은 '가공하지 않은', '날것'이라고 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for raw material that has been worked on, as in '가공식품' (processed food). If a photo or video is '가공되다', it also means it was edited so it differs from the original. Something untouched is described as '가공하지 않은' or '날것' (raw).

en: return (to a job, team, or original place)

examples.en: I return to the office tomorrow after my vacation.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 다친 뒤 석 달 만에 경기에 복귀했어요.
examples.en: The player returned to games three months after his injury.
It is time for the soldier to return to his unit.

examples.ko: 예전 일상으로 복귀하는 게 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It is not easy to get back to my old routine.

examples.ko: 병이 나으면 바로 학교에 복귀할 거예요.
examples.en: Once I recover, I will go back to school right away.
The singer who made a comeback released a new song.

explain: '돌아가다'는 어디든 쓰지만 '복귀하다'는 원래 있던 자리, 일, 팀으로 돌아갈 때 써요. '업무에 복귀하다', '선수가 복귀하다'처럼 자주 들려요. 집으로 돌아가는 것은 '복귀하다'가 아니라 '돌아가다', '귀가하다'예요.
explain_en: '돌아가다' can be used anywhere, but '복귀하다' is for going back to your original place, job, or team, as in '업무에 복귀하다' or '선수가 복귀하다'. Going back home is not '복귀하다' but '돌아가다' or '귀가하다'.

en: operate; manage (funds, systems); apply, put to use (a system)

examples.en: The bank manages its customers' money.

examples.ko: 이 동아리는 적은 회비를 아껴서 운용하고 있어요.
examples.en: This club manages its small membership fees carefully.
You need practice to operate the system well.

examples.ko: 회사가 새 제도를 운용한 지 1년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been a year since the company began running the new system.
How are you going to manage the money you have?
That department operates fifty computer servers.

explain: 돈, 장비, 제도를 목적에 맞게 잘 움직일 때 써요. 가게나 회사를 꾸려 갈 때는 '운영하다'가 더 자연스러워요. 기계를 손으로 직접 다룰 때는 '조작하다'를 써요.
explain_en: Use it for putting money, equipment, or a system to work toward a goal. For running a shop or company, '운영하다' sounds more natural. For handling a machine by hand, use '조작하다'.

examples.en: Our teacher coaches our team.

examples.ko: 아버지가 어릴 때 제게 수영을 코치해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father coached me in swimming when I was little.

examples.ko: 면접 대답을 코치해 줄 사람이 필요해요.
examples.en: I need someone to coach me on my interview answers.

examples.ko: 그는 십 년 동안 선수들을 코치했어요.
examples.en: He coached players for ten years.
I go to coach children in basketball every weekend.
I want to learn how to coach people.

explain: 일상에서는 '가르치다'가 더 흔하고, '코치하다'는 운동이나 면접처럼 기술을 옆에서 봐 주는 상황에 써요. 코치를 부를 때는 '코치님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: In daily speech '가르치다' is more common; '코치하다' fits situations where someone guides your skill from beside you, like sports or interview practice. You address a coach as '코치님'.

examples.ko: 그 회사는 만드는 방식을 완전히 혁신했어요.
examples.en: That company completely overhauled the way it makes things.
People who want to reform the school system gathered.

examples.ko: 새로운 기술이 우리 생활을 혁신하고 있어요.
examples.en: New technology is transforming our lives.
I think the outdated system should be reformed.
I changed the whole menu to revamp the shop.
It takes courage to innovate.

explain: '바꾸다'는 어떤 변화에도 쓰지만, '혁신하다'는 낡은 방식을 크게, 완전히 새롭게 바꾼다는 무거운 느낌이에요. 회사, 제도, 기술 같은 큰 대상에 써요. 작은 물건을 바꿀 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: '바꾸다' works for any kind of change, but '혁신하다' feels heavy: changing an old way of doing things greatly and completely. It is used for big things like companies, systems, and technology, not for swapping small objects.

examples.en: The player broke through the defense and scored a goal.

examples.ko: 우리 영화가 관객 천만 명을 돌파했어요.
examples.en: Our movie passed ten million viewers.
Let's get through this hard time together.
I pushed through the snowy road and barely arrived.

examples.ko: 이번 달 판매량이 목표를 돌파할 거예요.
examples.en: This month's sales will surpass the target.
I found a way to break through the crisis.

explain: 장애물이나 어려움을 뚫고 지나갈 때, 숫자가 기준을 넘을 때 둘 다 써요. '관객 천만 돌파', '인구 5천만 돌파'처럼 뉴스 제목에 자주 나와요. 그냥 넘는 것은 '넘다', 힘껏 뚫고 나아가는 느낌이면 '돌파하다'예요.
explain_en: It is used both for pushing through an obstacle and for a number passing a mark. News headlines often say '관객 천만 돌파' (passes ten million viewers). '넘다' is plain crossing; '돌파하다' has the feel of forcing your way through.

examples.en: The universe looks infinite.
Children's imagination is limitless.
I am grateful to my parents for their boundless love.
The possibilities are endless, so don't give up.

examples.ko: 자원이 무한하지 않아서 아껴 써야 해요.
examples.en: Resources are not unlimited, so we must save them.

examples.ko: 무한할 것 같던 에너지가 어느새 다 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The energy that seemed endless ran out before I knew it.

explain: 반대말은 '유한하다'인데 일상에서는 잘 쓰지 않고, 보통 '끝이 없다', '한이 없다'라고 말해요. '무한한 사랑', '무한한 가능성'처럼 명사 앞에 오는 모양이 많아요. 식당 간판의 '무한 리필'에서도 자주 봐요.
explain_en: The opposite is '유한하다', but it is rarely used in daily life; people usually say '끝이 없다' (there is no end). It often appears before nouns, as in '무한한 사랑' (boundless love) or '무한한 가능성'. You also see it on restaurant signs as '무한 리필' (unlimited refills).

examples.en: He affirmed that what I said was right.
If you accept yourself, your mind feels at ease.

examples.ko: 그 의견을 긍정하는 사람이 점점 많아졌어요.
examples.en: More and more people came to agree with that opinion.
I answered yes to the question with a nod.

examples.ko: 선생님이 제 노력을 긍정해 주셔서 기뻤어요.
examples.en: I was happy that my teacher recognized my effort.
You need to decide whether to affirm or deny the fact.

explain: 반대말은 '부정하다'예요. 어떤 말이나 사실이 맞다고 인정할 때 쓰지만, 말할 때는 '맞다고 하다', '인정하다'를 더 자주 써요. '긍정적이다'는 생각이 밝고 좋은 쪽이라는 뜻으로 훨씬 흔해요.
explain_en: The opposite is '부정하다'. It means to accept that something is true, but in speech people more often say '맞다고 하다' or '인정하다'. The related '긍정적이다' (positive, optimistic) is much more common.

examples.ko: 시청이 다음 달에 마라톤 대회를 주최해요.
examples.en: The city hall hosts a marathon next month.
Our school organized a speech contest.
Do you know who organized this event?

examples.ko: 회사에서 가족 초청 행사를 주최할 거예요.
examples.en: The company will host a family invitation event.

examples.ko: 행사를 주최하는 사람은 준비할 게 많아요.
examples.en: The person organizing an event has a lot to prepare.
I went to the festival organized by the city.

explain: 행사를 계획하고 여는 쪽을 '주최'라고 해요. 돈이나 물건으로 돕는 쪽은 '후원하다', 실제 운영을 맡는 쪽은 '주관하다'라서 서로 달라요. 집에서 파티를 열 때는 '열다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: The side that plans and holds an event is the '주최'. The side that helps with money or goods is '후원하다' (sponsors), and the side that runs it in practice is '주관하다', so they differ. For a party at home, '열다' (to hold) is more natural.

en: enact; establish (a law, rule, or day)

examples.en: The National Assembly enacted a new law.
The city established an Environment Day.
The school will establish a new rule.

examples.ko: 회사가 안전 수칙을 제정한 뒤 사고가 줄었어요.
examples.en: Accidents decreased after the company set safety rules.

examples.ko: 법을 제정하려면 많은 사람의 동의가 필요해요.
examples.en: To enact a law, you need the agreement of many people.

examples.ko: 우리 동아리는 지금 회칙을 제정하는 중이에요.
examples.en: Our club is in the middle of drawing up its bylaws.

explain: 법, 규칙, 기념일처럼 공식적인 것을 새로 만들어 정할 때 써요. '규칙을 만들다'가 일상 말이고, '제정하다'는 문서나 뉴스에 어울려요. 비슷하게 생긴 '개정하다'는 이미 있는 것을 고친다는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It is used when officially creating and fixing something new, such as a law, rule, or commemorative day. '규칙을 만들다' is the everyday phrase, while '제정하다' suits documents and news. The similar-looking '개정하다' differs: it revises something that already exists.

examples.en: Medical technology is advancing quickly.
The child's drawing skill has improved beyond recognition.
The more science advances, the more convenient things there are.

examples.ko: 많이 진보한 기술 덕분에 먼 곳과 쉽게 연락해요.
examples.en: Thanks to advanced technology, we can easily contact faraway places.
Even if you progress slowly, don't give up.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 예전 것보다 훨씬 진보했어요.
examples.en: This machine is much more advanced than the old one.

explain: 기술이나 실력이 더 나아질 때 써요. 일상에서는 '발전하다'가 더 흔하고, 사람의 실력은 '늘다'를 많이 써요. '진보'는 정치에서 '보수'의 반대말로도 쓰여서, 뉴스에서는 그 뜻일 때도 많아요.
explain_en: It means getting better, as with technology or skill. In daily talk '발전하다' is more common, and for a person's ability people often say '늘다'. '진보' is also used in politics as the opposite of '보수' (conservative), so in the news it often has that meaning.

examples.en: The police lifted the road closure.
To unlock the phone, you enter the password.
The government announced that it would lift the alert.

examples.ko: 계약을 해제하고 싶으면 일주일 전에 말해 주세요.
examples.en: If you want to cancel the contract, tell us a week in advance.
I heard they lifted the heavy rain advisory because the rain stopped.

examples.ko: 이 구역의 출입 제한을 오늘부터 해제해요.
examples.en: We are lifting the entry restriction on this area starting today.

explain: 묶이거나 막혀 있던 것을 풀 때 써요. '잠금 해제', '경보 해제', '계약 해제'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 어느 정도 정해져 있어요. 매듭이나 문제를 푸는 '풀다'와 달리 제도, 기능, 상태를 대상으로 해요.
explain_en: It is used when releasing something that was tied or blocked. Common pairings are '잠금 해제' (unlock), '경보 해제' (alert lifted), and '계약 해제' (contract cancellation). Unlike '풀다', which is for untying a knot or solving a problem, '해제하다' targets rules, functions, and states.

examples.en: The main character's daughter was kidnapped in the movie.

examples.ko: 납치될 뻔한 아이를 지나가던 사람이 구했어요.
examples.en: A passerby saved the child who almost got kidnapped.

examples.ko: 어제 뉴스에서 납치된 사람이 무사히 돌아왔다고 했어요.
examples.en: The news yesterday said the kidnapped person came back safely.
Parents are careful so that children do not get kidnapped.

examples.ko: 그는 납치돼서 사흘 동안 갇혀 있었어요.
examples.en: He was kidnapped and held for three days.

examples.ko: 그 소설에는 왕자가 납치되는 장면이 나와요.
examples.en: There is a scene in that novel where the prince is kidnapped.

explain: 사람을 억지로 데려가는 일이라 주로 뉴스, 영화, 소설에서 들려요. 하는 쪽은 '납치하다', 당하는 쪽은 '납치되다'예요. '데려가다'와 달리 몰래, 강제로 한다는 느낌이 강해요.
explain_en: Because it means a person is taken away by force, you mostly hear it in news, movies, and novels. The one doing it uses '납치하다', and the one it happens to uses '납치되다'. Unlike '데려가다' (take along), it strongly implies secrecy and force.
